entry_item.definition: T. lus (honorific)sku; S.kāya. Body, person. The M. word has through the T. absorbed certain special meanings of S. kāya, such as 'group, mass, aspect.” For bej-e as the internal base see tøryn tygeky.

example.definition: T. lus dran pa; S. kāya-smrti. Mindfulness of the parts of the body, one of the four kinds of mindfulness.

example.unicode: ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠨ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠯ ~ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠯ
example.definition: T. lus, skad, yid (or honor.) sku, bkah, thugs; S. kāya, vāk, citta. Body , speech, and mind, the three mystical constituents of the personality in esoterism. To realize under this triple aspect one's own personality as identical (With the deity) is the most essential requirement for the successful performance of bytygel yn arγ-a

T. sku gsum (bzhi); S. tri-kāya, (catuh-kāya). The Bu. was believed having three (four ) bodies or basic aspects, namely: xubilγan-u bej-e, T. sprul sku, S. nirmāna-kāya, a 'magical, apparitional, docetic body' by which he appeared to amitan; zirγalantu bej-e, T. long spyod kyi sku, S. sambhoga-kāya, a 'body of bliss' , 'enjoyment body', 'beatific body' which he enjoyes in paradise; and a nom un bej-e, T. chos kyi sku, S. dharma-kāya, which may be roughly described as the 'absolute deified.' For the fourth body see Vacirdar-a.
